outline_section.section_title: Introduction to Convolution of Two Equal-Width Rectangular Pulses
outline_section.learning_goal: Recognize that convolving two equal-width rectangular pulses reduces to tracking a sliding overlap length and scaling that length by the pulse heights.

image_policy.image_description_seed: Show two equal-width rectangular pulses on a tau-axis: a fixed support for x(tau), a flipped-and-shifted support for h(t - tau), and the overlap interval that changes as t increases.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach the base schema for equal-width rectangular-pulse convolution: the integral is determined by where the two supports overlap in the convolution variable.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Two equal-width rectangular pulses of width T, with x(tau) fixed on 0 <= tau <= T and h(t - tau) sliding across it as t changes.
paragraph_plan: Introduce the convolution integral and identify tau as the variable used to compare the fixed pulse with the shifted pulse.
Explain that the rectangular pulses are constant on their supports, so the integrand is nonzero only on the overlap of those supports.
Name the three structural events for equal widths: first contact, peak alignment, and last contact.
Preview the output shape: the overlap length rises linearly, then falls linearly, producing a triangular convolution output.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Keep the tutorial compact: define the geometric overlap interpretation before any piecewise computation.

prompt_blocks.text: Two unit-height rectangular pulses have equal width 4. The fixed support is x(tau) nonzero on 0 <= tau <= 4, and h(t - tau) has moving support [t - 4, t]. Which ordered list gives first contact, peak alignment, and last contact?

question.correct_answer: First contact occurs at t = 0, peak alignment at t = 4, and last contact at t = 8.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The fixed support is [0, 4] and the moving support is [t - 4, t]. First contact occurs when the right edge t reaches 0, peak alignment occurs when [t - 4, t] = [0, 4], and last contact occurs when t - 4 = 4.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 5, x(tau) is fixed on 0 <= tau <= 5 and h(t - tau) is supported on [t - 5, t]. What is the overlap length L(t) for 0 <= t <= 5?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the rising interval, t - 5 is at or to the left of 0 and t is inside [0, 5]. The overlap is therefore [0, t], so its length is t - 0 = t.

prompt_blocks.text: For two equal-width rectangular pulses of width 5, x(tau) is fixed on 0 <= tau <= 5 and h(t - tau) is supported on [t - 5, t]. What is the overlap length L(t) for 5 <= t <= 10?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: On the falling interval, t - 5 is inside [0, 5] and t is at or to the right of 5. The overlap is therefore [t - 5, 5], so its length is 5 - (t - 5) = 10 - t.
